# Surface InferenceService deployment status in Dashboard model serving views

## Description

Deliver a deployment status indicator (Ready, Progressing, Failed) for every deployed model in the Dashboard's model serving views, so data scientists can tell whether a KServe InferenceService deployment is healthy without leaving the console or running `oc` commands. The status must reflect the actual InferenceService state within 30 seconds of a change, without a manual page reload.

## Scope

- Add a deployment status field (Ready / Progressing / Failed) to the deployed models list and model serving detail views in the Dashboard.
- Derive the displayed status from the InferenceService CR status conditions and recent Kubernetes events exposed by KServe (serving.kserve.io/v1beta1), per the Dashboard's existing pattern of reading component CRs through the Kubernetes API.
- Include the passive-component validation: verify the existing KServe InferenceService status conditions are sufficient to distinguish all three displayed statuses; if a state cannot be derived from existing conditions, that is a defect to resolve (fix-and-retry), not a scope change.
- Status refresh path so the displayed state tracks the actual InferenceService state within 30 seconds of a change, without requiring a manual page reload.
- Incidental updates to existing view captions or references that fall out of this change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a deployed model whose InferenceService is Ready, When the user views the model serving list or model detail, Then a "Ready" status is displayed for that model.
- Given a deployment that is progressing or failed, When the user views the model serving views, Then "Progressing" or "Failed" is displayed respectively.
- Given a change in the InferenceService's actual state, When 30 seconds have elapsed, Then the displayed status reflects the new state without a manual page reload (HLR-3, measured by observing the UI after a state change with no reload).
- The status derivation for each InferenceService state (Ready, Progressing, Failed) is verified against the condition set KServe exposes on the InferenceService status; any state that cannot be represented is fixed before completion.
- Existing model serving views are not regressed (existing list, detail, and deployment flows still function).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): status visible per deployed model in model serving views.
- HLR-3 (P1): status reflects actual state within 30 seconds, no manual reload (bundled here — same data path and views as HLR-1; splitting would duplicate the same implementation surface).

# Deployment status detail view: condition messages and recent events

## Description

Deliver a status detail view in the Dashboard that a user can open for a failed or progressing model deployment, showing the underlying InferenceService condition messages and the recent Kubernetes events for that deployment. This turns "my model has been Pending for an hour" support cases into self-service diagnosis: the information the platform already has becomes visible in the console.

## Scope

- Add a status detail view (or expandable panel) reachable from the deployment status shown in the model serving views, for deployments in Failed or Progressing state.
- Surface the InferenceService CR status condition messages (e.g. Ready, PredictorReady conditions with reasons and messages).
- Surface the recent Kubernetes events associated with the deployment.
- Read all data through the Dashboard's existing Kubernetes API access pattern; no new private component APIs.
- Incidental updates to captions or references that fall out of this change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a deployment in Failed or Progressing state, When the user opens the status detail view, Then the underlying condition messages for that InferenceService are displayed.
- Given a deployment with recent Kubernetes events, When the user opens the status detail view, Then those recent events are displayed (measured by comparing the view against `oc describe`/`oc get events` output for the same InferenceService).
- Given a deployment in Ready state, When the user views the model serving views, Then the detail view either is not offered or shows the same data consistently with the Ready status.
- The view renders for InferenceService deployments in both serverless and raw deployment modes (KServe InferenceService scope; ModelMesh deployments are out of scope).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): status detail view showing condition messages and recent events for failed or progressing deployments.

# Filter and sort the deployed models list by status

## Description

Extend the Dashboard's deployed models list so users can filter the list to a chosen deployment status (Ready, Progressing, Failed) and sort it by status. This lets data scientists quickly find failed deployments in projects with many models.

## Scope

- Add status-based filtering controls to the deployed models list view.
- Add status-based sorting to the deployed models list view.
- Reuse the deployment status field already surfaced on the list; no new data path is introduced.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a list of deployed models with mixed statuses, When the user filters by a status, Then only models with that status are displayed.
- Given a list of deployed models, When the user sorts by status, Then the list is ordered by the status values.
- Filtering and sorting compose correctly with each other and do not regress existing list behavior.
- The list view reflects the same status values shown elsewhere in the model serving views (no divergence between the filter options and the displayed statuses).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): users can filter and sort the deployed models list by status.
